title: operational-play-patterns-access-procurement-travel-2029
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This play-patterns guide consolidates core company-wide processes for: access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, and travel. Its goal is to present consistent operational patterns teams can copy/adapt, reduce friction for cross-functional requests, and ensure compliance with legal and security requirements. Use this as a canonical reference and toolkit (with templates) for day-to-day operations.

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors with corporate accounts, and teams operating Redwood-managed systems. Exceptions (e.g., regulated customers or air-gapped private deployments) are noted inline.

Principles
----------
- Least privilege by default: access must be minimal and time-bound.
- Separation of duties: approval owners differ from executors.
- Auditability: every change or procurement recordable in a system of record.
- Risk-based flexibility: higher-risk actions require higher review bar and longer lead time.

Key roles and responsibilities
------------------------------
- Requestor: initiates access/change/procurement/travel request and supplies justification.
- Approver(s): team manager / data owner / finance approver as listed in approval matrix.
- Executor: person or team that performs the change or places the order.
- Compliance owner: validates controls for vendors and high-sensitivity data.
- Process owner: Finance & Legal (for procurement/expenses); Security (access/data); SRE (environment changes).

1) Access & Permissions
------------------------
Policy summary:
- All access to production systems requires ticketed approval and one-time 2FA verification.
- Privileged roles (DB admin, infra-admin, signing key owners) require quarterly attestation.
- Temporary access defaults to a 7-day expiration unless explicitly extended.

Request workflow (standard access):
1. Requestor files an access request in the access system (UI/ServiceNow/Jira template).
2. Manager approves for business justification.
3. Resource owner or Security reviews and grants, setting an expiration.
4. Requestor confirms access and documents the change in the ticket.

Approval matrix (summary):
| Resource type | Manager approval | Security review | Finance sign-off | Expiry defaults |
|--------------|------------------|-----------------|------------------|-----------------|
| Repo (non-prod) | Team lead | Optional | No | 30 days |
| Prod service console | Team lead + Eng manager | Required | No | 7 days |
| Billing portal | Finance lead | Optional | Required | 30 days |

SLOs and metrics:
- Standard access requests: 48 business hours target for approval.
- Emergency access (see below): immediate escalation; post-facto attestation within 3 business days.

Emergency access pattern:
- For incidents requiring immediate access, follow the emergency-access runbook: paging Security on-call, temporary grant for incident responders for up to 4 hours, and mandatory post-incident audit.

Sample access request (JSON payload for automation):
{
  "requestor": "alice@redwood.com",
  "resource": "production-kv-store",
  "role": "read-write",
  "justification": "Investigating data mismatch for feature rollout",
  "duration_hours": "72"
}

2) Change Management
---------------------
Classification:
- Standard change: low risk, pre-approved templates, no downtime.
- Planned change: requires scheduling, stakeholder notification, and rollback plan.
- Emergency change: immediate for incident mitigation; requires post-facto review.

Planned change checklist (minimum):
1. Description & business justification.
2. Backout plan and test plan.
3. Stakeholder list (including SRE, product owner, legal if customer-impacting).
4. Scheduled window and monitoring plan.
5. Approval signoffs (Engineering manager, SRE owner).
6. Post-deploy validation checklist.

Rollback procedure (sample):
1. Detect failure through monitoring alert -> SRE page.
2. Trigger backout plan; announce to stakeholders.
3. If rollback fails, escalate to incident management and apply incident playbook.

Change window policy:
- Standard maintenance windows: Tue/Thu 02:00–05:00 UTC for non-customer-impacting infra changes. Customer-facing releases require a 72-hour pre-notice unless explicitly waived by product leadership.

3) Data Management (classification + handling)
--------------------------------------------
Classification levels:
- PUBLIC: can be shared externally.
- INTERNAL: non-sensitive internal materials.
- CONFIDENTIAL: PII, customer data, secrets.
- RESTRICTED: regulated data (HIPAA/PCI-equivalent), requires extra controls.

Handling rules (summary):
- Encryption-in-transit and at-rest required for CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED.
- Limit exports: CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data export requires Data Owner approval and an approved DPA clause for vendor transfers.
- Retention: follow the Data Retention Schedule (see related page).

Data breach steps (brief):
1. Contain & identify scope.
2. Notify Security & Legal within 4 hours.
3. Triage, remediate, and start notification timeline as required by law/customer contract.

4) Procurement & Expenses
-------------------------
Procurement thresholds and approvals (table):
| Amount (USD) | Approvals required | Notes |
|-------------:|-------------------|-------|
| <= 5,000 | Team lead | Purchase request (PR) via procurement form |
| 5,001–50,000 | Dept head + Finance | PO issued; vendor terms reviewed by Legal if > 25k |
| > 50,000 | VP + Finance Director + Legal | Formal contract review and board notice for multi-year commitments |

Procurement pattern (recommended):
1. Use procurement template (link at bottom) to capture vendor, justification, TCO, and exit terms.
2. Finance verifies budget and issues PO.
3. Legal reviews contracts per thresholds.
4. Vendor onboarding security questionnaire if any CONFIDENTIAL data will be shared.

Expense & travel policy highlights:
- Use corporate cards or expense portal. Receipts mandatory for items > 25 USD.
- Per-diem for domestic travel: 80 USD/day; international per-diem uses government rates.
- Travel approval: manager + travel coordinator for >2 nights or international.
- Reimbursements processed within 10 business days after submission.

CLI example: create a PR (internal procurement tool)
$ rwpurchase create --vendor "DataStream Inc" --amount 12000 --cost-center ENG-ML --justification "Telemetry pipeline"

5) Vendor Management
---------------------
Onboarding checklist:
- Vendor information form completed (legal entity, tax IDs, contacts).
- Security questionnaire for data access completed and reviewed by Security.
- Contract & SLA finalized and stored in contract registry.
- Finance setup (W-9/Invoice details) and PO terms assigned.
- Assigned account owner inside Redwood and runbook for offboarding.

Security baseline for vendors accessing CONFIDENTIAL data:
- SOC2 Type II or equivalent, or compensating controls documented.
- Minimum encryption, MFA for vendor accounts, and least-privilege access.
- Quarterly review cadence for critical vendors.

Vendor risk escalation:
- If security gaps identified, pause data sharing, notify Vendor Owner and Security, and remediate within 15 business days.

6) Travel & Expenses (operational guidance)
------------------------------------------
Pre-travel checklist:
1. Manager approval for travel with dates and purpose.
2. Book through approved vendor/travel portal for insurance coverage.
3. Submit estimated expenses to expense portal if requesting an advance.

Expense submission pattern:
1. Submit receipt, expense category, and client/meeting notes within 30 days of expense.
2. Manager approves; Finance reconciles against per-diem and policy rules.

Disallowed expenses (examples): personal entertainment, first-class upgrades without pre-approval, household items.

7) Templates and toolkit
------------------------
Attached templates (copy/adapt):
- access-request-template.md (fields: resource, role, justification, duration, impacted-services)
- change-plan-template.md (fields: owner, backout, test-plan, stakeholders)
- procurement-request-template.yaml (fields: vendor, sku, cost, contract-term, exit-clause)
- vendor-onboarding-checklist.xlsx
- travel-expense-form.pdf

Sample procurement-request-template.yaml snippet:
---
vendor: "DataStream Inc"
items:
  - sku: DS-PIPE-1
    description: Telemetry pipeline (managed)
    cost_usd: 12000
cost_center: ENG-ML
justification: "Replace legacy aggregator for lower egress costs"
contract_term_months: 12
---
